newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ABARE cuts Australia 1996/97 lead forecast.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ABARE cuts Australia 1996/97 lead forecast.

text.p: Australian lead mine output is expected to rise two percent to 515,000 tonnes in the 1996/97 year to June 30 but this is down on the September forecast of 520,000, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said in its December quarterly report.
The higher output is due to MIM Holdings Ltd's McArthur River mine in Northern Territory, the government commodities forecaster said.

"Higher export volumes of refined lead and lead bullion, together with the expected increase in world lead prices, are forecast to result in Australian lead export earnings rising by almost 11 percent to A$504 million in 1996/97," the bureau said.

ABARE also forecasts world lead mine production to rise, by 3.9 percent percent to 5.83 million tonnes in calendar 1997. Production in 1996 is estimated at 5.61 million tonnes compared with 5.43 million in 1995.
The bureau said consumption was forecast to rise to 5.88 million tonnes in calendar 1997 from an estimated 5.71 million in 1996, which is up on the 5.56 million consumed in 1995.
ABARE said lead prices were expected to rise further in the 1997 year, after an estimated 23 percent increase in 1996.
ABARE forecasts lead prices to average US$870 per tonne in 1997, compared with $777 in 1996.

"With world lead consumption exceeding world production in 1996, and forecast to do so again in 1997, average prices are forecast to increase by a further 12 percent to $870 per tonne (US$0.39/lb) in 1997 as stocks continue to decline," ABARE said.
ABARE said lead stockpiles were expected to fall to four weeks consumption in 1997, from an estimated 4.2 weeks in 1996, which is down on the average 4.7 weeks in 1995.
